data.hypothesis: The prior lead-directed and shared-loop scalar variants measured slower than baseline, while predicate aggregation was valid and very close to baseline; these results do not establish that branch reduction helps. This pure-scalar experiment uses byte classes and a compact transition table to replace width-specific decoding branches while retaining an ASCII-run fast path. It tests whether simpler transitions outweigh the class/transition lookup dependencies. A prior DFA development attempt failed correctness, so this version explicitly represents restricted second-byte classes; performance remains unmeasured.

memory_lessons.applicability: Comparing scalar UTF-8 decoder variants on this mixed-width workload.
memory_lessons.claim: The predicate-aggregation candidate measured 49.545 µs versus the baseline's 49.623 µs, whereas the lead-directed and shared-continuation-loop candidates measured 56.50 µs and 61.73 µs. These measurements do not isolate the cause or establish a repeatable benefit from reduced branching.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a distinct compact-state implementation and verify official ASCII and malformed-input cases before comparing performance.

memory_lessons.applicability: When rebuilding a compact-state UTF-8 decoder.
memory_lessons.claim: A prior compact-state DFA development attempt failed protected correctness checks; a DFA structure alone is not evidence of validity.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check restricted second-byte ranges and incomplete sequences with the controller's official correctness suite.

data.notes: This is a pure-scalar table-driven DFA variant, not a hybrid. The supplied catalog reports three distinct measured programs and no repeats. The earlier DFA attempt failed development correctness and has no performance result; this candidate is separately constructed with explicit continuation subranges. No speedup is claimed; controller correctness and performance evaluation are needed.
transformations: Replaced scalar width-specific decoding with a byte-class table and compact transition table, including distinct continuation subranges for restricted second-byte validation.
Retained an ASCII-run fast path while state is accepting; rejected invalid transitions immediately and rejected incomplete sequences at end of input.
Preserved the existing run ABI and output assignment.
